note: Exceptions for scripts/check-glossary-terms.mjs. `include` is the doc set that carries Wynding's game vocabulary; ADRs and design-notes are deliberately out of scope — they are engineering prose, where these words (save, layer, field, digest) carry their ordinary technical senses and would cost far more exceptions than the drift they would catch. `ignoredTerms` are avoided words whose other sense cannot be told apart mechanically. `allowedSenses` are case-insensitive regexes over a line of prose: a hit inside a match is a different sense, not drift; keep them narrow, since a loose pattern exempts the next real violation on the same line. Every entry states why; an entry that matches nothing fails the check. See docs/ai-workflow.md.

ignoredTerms.why: The glossary itself allows it: "interchangeable in prose, but 'path' is canonical in code" — so linting it in docs would contradict the entry it comes from.
Unavoidable generic English in these docs — grid unit, fixed-point units, unit of work, unit-tested. Telling those from 'unit' meaning a tower needs grammar, not grep.
Every use here is the verb ("shapes the route by building", "Building is allowed while paused"). Only the noun is drift, and a grep cannot tell them apart.
Engine is itself a canonical term (the determinism toolkit), so flagging the word would tell an author to rename the thing it is named after. Only "engine" meaning the sim is drift.
A save is its own concept per the Replay entry's aside and ADR 0008 — a state snapshot. Only calling a replay a save is drift, and that reads identically to a grep.
The ordinary verb ("update the HUD", "an app update") is everywhere; only "update" meaning one tick is drift.

allowedSenses.why: "Core Gameplay" is PRD 0001's title and "core loop" is the game's central loop — neither names the engine package.
The deterministic/byte-identity/web core is the codebase's centre in the ordinary sense, not the Engine package being renamed.
Modelling prose — the damage, grid, domain, or multi-wave state model is a set of rules, not the sim package.
The genre name ("tower defense", "fixed-lane defense") and the player's defenses as a whole — not armor, the stat.
Names the whole damage system in PRD 0001 §5; the stat inside it is still called armor.
A tower's upgrade level, and the two granularity suffixes the specs use (tick-level, milestone-level) — not a board, wave, or difficulty tier.
The pathfinding algorithm (flow-field + A*) and its per-tick derivation phase, not the board.
The data-record sense — a schema field, the field a buff modifies, the five axis fields of a creep.
A creep durability stat, per the Creep entry's own wording. Score is the thing that must not be called points.
Geometry: creeps are points on the fine grid.

allowedSenses.pattern: hp pips?|creep[/ ]hp|\(hp, damage|durability = hp|\| hp\b|max hp|hp-fraction
allowedSenses.why: The glossary's own note — HP is a creep stat: its table column, its durability axis, its render fraction. Deliberately narrow, so "the player's HP" and "0 HP left" keep failing. `pips?` (not just the plural) covers the accessibility checklist's singular "HP pip"; `creep[/ ]hp` covers both "creep HP" and "creep/HP-pip".

A wave launches, auto-launches, or is launched by an early call — the wave-start sense, not a release. Deliberately requires the wave to be launching or be launched: "we launch after the last wave" is still drift.

allowedSenses.pattern: Launch & spawn spacing|launch \+ \d+ ticks|launch tick|auto-launch(es|ed|ing)?|countdown before launch|wave timing chains off the previous\s+launch|launch itself — spawns|start at launch, offset
allowedSenses.why: The wave-start sense, named construction by construction — never a bare "(before|at|previous|the) launch", which would equally exempt a release-sense sentence (issue #65): the m1.md bold list-item lead-in "Launch & spawn spacing", the tick-offset math "launch + 180 ticks", the launch tick, an auto-launch on countdown expiry, the countdown before launch, wave timing that CHAINS OFF THE PREVIOUS launch (not a bare "previous launch"), the launch itself immediately followed by what it does ("— spawns", not a bare "launch itself"), and the mixed-wave stream-offset default ("start at launch, offset", not a bare "at launch"). "Ships at launch" and "the product launch itself is delayed" are still drift. Two residuals found in review and closed: `launch + N` is now `launch + N ticks` (it would otherwise have exempted "the product launch + 3 weeks of polish"), and the chains-off form now requires its wave subject.
The adjective — "high durability", "one high-impact discharge". Written as a negative, so the grading sense the P0–P3 entry rejects ("high severity", "high-priority") is not exempted and still fails.
Medium is a difficulty-tier name (Easy/Medium/Hard), not a severity label. Kept linted rather than ignored so "medium severity" still fails.
The Phase entry's own definition — "a coherent stage of the product" — defining the canonical term in plain English.
Something delivered in a phase or release line, not a milestone renamed.
The elemental damage-type system PRD 0001 rules out — not a creep's domain.

The catalog sense — more tower/creep types, the wave preview's "creep types and counts", one creep type in the M1 slice. Deliberately narrow: "each creep type is ground or air" is domain drift and still fails.
Structural senses — the product has a frame, a tick has an outer frame of phases — not a rendered frame.

The rendered sense, which CONTEXT.md's Tick entry itself calls a render concept and bars only as a SYNONYM for 'tick'. The entry above covers the structural senses; this one covers the render-side compounds m2.md needs from M2-S4b on, hyphenated or spaced: the spike reports 95th-percentile frame time against a frame-rate floor. A frame time is emphatically not a tick — the whole point of the render/sim decoupling is that they are different clocks — so calling it a tick would be the actual drift. Kept to these compounds so a bare 'frame' meaning a tick still trips.
A fresh layer of tuning, and the presentation layer of the app — not a creep's domain.
The sim's scheduled-impact event queue, not a player command awaiting a tick.
The severity entry says there is no P4 — it has to name it to rule it out.
The Creep entry defines the canonical term in plain English.
Early-call score credit, the scoring component the glossary's Early call entry names. "80 credits" for currency is still drift — that is what the Bounty entry rejects.
The adjective — "low-end device". Written as a negative, so the grading sense ("low severity", "low-priority") still fails.
The app's two responsive layouts (Standard and Compact, ADR 0003 / M1 story 11), not a maze.
The ruleset's runtime load path — when loading happens, not the Engine package.
The status-effect framework — a named subsystem of the sim, not the Engine package.
The ruleset digest of ADR 0007, a different hash from the world-hash; the glossary's own aside allows the word in prose.
axe-core is the accessibility-testing tool's own name (docs/accessibility-checklist.md, ADR 0003 §3), not the Engine package.

allowedSenses.pattern: app-shell layout|Shell/Rail/Card/Panel/Dock layout|in BOTH layouts|Both layouts already|two layouts|Compact layout|layout/interaction story|New layout states|layout/topology change|Neither layout|declared layout region
allowedSenses.why: The app's Standard/Compact responsive UI layout system, construction by construction. `both layouts` is anchored to "in BOTH layouts" — bare, it would exempt "both layouts funnel creeps into a corridor", which IS the maze sense.
The deferred cue-geometry design pass this checklist repeatedly refers back to (Story 6/8's PARTIAL rows) — an arrangement of render radii, not a maze.

allowedSenses.pattern: colour[- ]?blind modes?|colour[- ]modes?|colour-vision modes?|tritan value sits closer to that mode
allowedSenses.why: The selectable colour-vision modes (protan/deutan/tritan/default), not a difficulty tier. The last alternative ties the bare "that mode's" back to the tritan/colour-mode sentence it refers to, rather than exempting a bare "mode".
Ordinary software idioms — a UI failure mode, a dev-mode console warning — not a difficulty tier.

allowedSenses.pattern: Visible focus indicators|3px focus indicator|focus indicators? \(WCAG
allowedSenses.why: WCAG's own term for the visible focus ring (2.4.7 Focus Visible), anchored to the conformance-row label and the WCAG citation — a bare `focus indicator` would exempt "the slowed effect's focus indicator", which IS telegraph drift.

allowedSenses.pattern: extended to also skip|skip to site|draw sites skip
allowedSenses.why: Three unrelated ordinary-English constructions, each anchored to its host clause: a Playwright project's testIgnore skipping specs, the conventional "skip to site" nav-link pattern, and a draw call skipping a null ring. A bare `to also skip` would exempt "choose to also skip the countdown", which IS the early-call sense.

Three unrelated senses: the Fullscreen API never trapping the user, WCAG's keyboard focus trap, and the ordinary "code trap" (a two-branch pitfall a mutation test catches) — none is the burst-tower sense.
Ordinary English compounds — Escape handling scoped to the whole game, a TypeScript type-system fact, and browser zoom percentage — none is a board, wave, or difficulty tier.
TypeScript's type system ("a type-level fact"), not a creep's domain.

allowedSenses.pattern: one layer at a time|paint layer
allowedSenses.why: Escape/Close backing out one modal/UI layer at a time, and the render paint layer (`drawCreeps`/`drawTowers`) — neither is a creep's domain.
Playwright's own test configuration (`playwright.config.ts`), not the ruleset.

allowedSenses.pattern: field, not two independent booleans|they read the same field|the field is proven to gate on data|the sixth field|six-field accessible text|every other Panel field
allowedSenses.why: The TowerStats/Panel schema sense. `read the same field` is anchored to its subject ("they read the same field") — bare, it would exempt "creeps entering from the north read the same field", which IS the board sense.
PLAN.md's own packet numbering (P1 through P4), not the review-severity scale that has no P4.
Display rounding precision (the Panel's shared one-decimal `formatNumber`), not the sim's internal fixed-point encoding.
The ordinary verb "to point at" (describing footprint-mark geometry, hand-wrapped across a line break so "at" was pulled up onto the same line as "points"), not the score sense.
"Not a copy nit" — an ordinary editorial-polish sense, not the P0–P3 review-severity scale's rejected grading term.

allowedSenses.pattern: literal-key map|label map|total-over-any-string map|re-maps the|maps to the|Both maps are unit-tested
allowedSenses.why: The JS lookup-table sense. `Both maps are` is anchored to "unit-tested" — bare, it would exempt "both maps are twenty by twelve", which IS the board sense.

allowedSenses.pattern: interaction model|Armed model|rotate model|sim-derived view model
allowedSenses.why: The UI-state sense. `view model` is anchored to "sim-derived view model" — bare, it would exempt "the view model of the world advances one step per tick", which IS the sim sense.

The test-double sense, anchored to its host clause. An earlier form allowed 25 arbitrary characters between "recording" and "double" — the loosest pattern in this file — which would have exempted "the recording plays back at double speed". Note the anchor cannot name the code span between them: this linter strips inline code before matching.

allowedSenses.pattern: health of the thing it is drawn on
allowedSenses.why: A recurring engineering maxim in this checklist (an essential cue must not depend on the condition of what it's drawn on) — applied to auras and towers as much as creeps, not the player's Lives.

allowedSenses.pattern: resizes the stage|over the Stage on Standard|painted bottom-left over the Stage|sub-400px stages
allowedSenses.why: The app's own named Stage element. `over the Stage` is anchored to its two host clauses — bare and case-insensitive, it would exempt "the rollout runs over the stage where we gate the beta", which IS the phase sense.

allowedSenses.pattern: QC round[\s-]?\d+|round[\s-]?\d+ (wrongly|noted|corrected)|taken in a review round|round-trip|Playtest polish round
allowedSenses.why: Review/QC round numbering and the serialize round-trip. `review round` is anchored to "taken in a review round" — bare, it would exempt "the review round of creeps arrives at tick 200", which IS the wave sense.

allowedSenses.pattern: rather than relying on a frame|frame that refreshes|every few frames
allowedSenses.why: The render-frame (rAF) sense. `relying on a frame` is anchored to "rather than relying on a frame" — bare, it would exempt "the sim advances by relying on a frame counter", which IS the tick sense.
